title: The Temptation and Jesus Rejected at Nazareth

questions.question: When Jesus returned from the Jordan, full of the Holy Spirit, how long was He led by the Spirit in the wilderness?
options: For forty days, being tempted by the devil
For thirty days, fasting and praying
For three days, sleeping in a cave
For seven days, preparing for His ministry
questions.correctAnswer: For forty days, being tempted by the devil
questions.explanation: Luke 4:1-2 (ESV): "And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted by the devil."

questions.question: What was the devil's first temptation to Jesus, appealing to His hunger?
options: "If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread."
"Turn this sand into manna."
"Ask angels to bring you food from heaven."
"Show me your power by eating this bitter fruit without harm."
questions.correctAnswer: "If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread."
questions.explanation: Luke 4:3 (ESV): "The devil said to him, 'If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.'"

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the temptation to turn the stone into bread?
options: "It is written, 'Man shall not live by bread alone.'"
"It is written, 'You shall worship the Lord your God.'"
"My food is to do the will of him who sent me."
"Only God provides bread in the desert."
questions.correctAnswer: "It is written, 'Man shall not live by bread alone.'"
questions.explanation: Luke 4:4 (ESV): "And Jesus answered him, 'It is written, "Man shall not live by bread alone."'"

questions.question: The devil took Him up and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. The devil offered Jesus all this authority and glory if Jesus would do what?
options: "If you, then, will worship me, it will all be yours."
"If you will deny your Father in heaven."
"If you will jump from the mountain and survive."
"If you will build a temple to me in Jerusalem."
questions.correctAnswer: "If you, then, will worship me, it will all be yours."
questions.explanation: Luke 4:7 (ESV): "If you, then, will worship me, it will all be yours."

questions.question: After Jesus rejected the third temptation (throwing Himself down from the temple), what did the devil do?
options: He departed from him until an opportune time
He screamed and vanished in smoke
He attacked Jesus physically but failed
He returned immediately to hell
questions.correctAnswer: He departed from him until an opportune time
questions.explanation: Luke 4:13 (ESV): "And when the devil had ended every temptation, he departed from him until an opportune time."

questions.question: Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and came to Nazareth where He was brought up. What was His custom on the Sabbath day?
options: He went to the synagogue, and he stood up to read
He rested peacefully at home
He gathered His disciples by the sea
He worked miracles in the market
questions.correctAnswer: He went to the synagogue, and he stood up to read
questions.explanation: Luke 4:16 (ESV): "And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. And as was his custom, he went to the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and he stood up to read."

questions.question: From which prophet was the scroll handed to Jesus to read?
options: Isaiah
Jeremiah
Ezekiel
Malachi
questions.explanation: Luke 4:17 (ESV): "And the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was given to him. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where it was written,"

questions.question: What did Jesus say after reading the prophecy from Isaiah beginning, "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me..."?
options: "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
"Tomorrow these things will come to pass."
"Blessed are those who wait upon the Lord."
"The prophet spoke of John, who prepares the way."
questions.correctAnswer: "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
questions.explanation: Luke 4:21 (ESV): "And he began to say to them, 'Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.'"

questions.question: Initially the people spoke well of Him, but then what question did they ask, showing their unbelief?
options: "Is not this Joseph's son?"
"Where did he learn perfectly to read?"
"Why is he wearing simple robes?"
"How can a man heal the sick?"
questions.explanation: Luke 4:22 (ESV): "And all spoke well of him and marveled at the gracious words that were coming from his mouth. And they said, 'Is not this Joseph's son?'"

questions.question: To illustrate that a prophet is unacceptable in his hometown, Jesus gave an example of Elijah being sent to a widow in Zarephath in the land of Sidon, and Elisha healing Naaman. What nationality was Naaman?
options: The Syrian
The Egyptian
The Roman
The Samaritan
questions.explanation: Luke 4:27 (ESV): "And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed, but only Naaman the Syrian."

questions.question: When they heard these things in the synagogue, how did the people in Nazareth react?
options: They were filled with wrath, drove him out of the town, and led him to the brow of the hill to throw him down the cliff
They fell down and wept in repentance
They argued with him until evening
They tore their clothes and declared him a blasphemer
questions.correctAnswer: They were filled with wrath, drove him out of the town, and led him to the brow of the hill to throw him down the cliff
questions.explanation: Luke 4:28-29 (ESV): "When they heard these things, all in the synagogue were filled with wrath. And they rose up and drove him out of the town and brought him to the brow of the hill... so that they could throw him down the cliff."

questions.question: How did Jesus escape the angry mob at Nazareth?
options: But passing through their midst, he went away
He called down fire from heaven to blind them
He was rescued by his disciples waiting below
He became invisible and walked away
questions.correctAnswer: But passing through their midst, he went away
questions.explanation: Luke 4:30 (ESV): "But passing through their midst, he went away."

questions.question: Jesus went down to Capernaum to teach on the Sabbath. What did the man possessed by a demon in the synagogue cry out?
options: "Ha! What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God."
"Mercy, Son of David, have mercy!"
"My name is Legion, for we are many."
"Get away from me, you man of fire!"
questions.correctAnswer: "Ha! What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God."
questions.explanation: Luke 4:34 (ESV): "Ha! What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God."

questions.question: Jesus arose from the synagogue and entered whose house, where he healed someone's mother-in-law of a high fever?
options: Simon's house
Andrew's house
Matthew's house
Zacchaeus's house
questions.explanation: Luke 4:38 (ESV): "And he arose and left the synagogue and entered Simon's house. Now Simon's mother-in-law was ill with a high fever,"

questions.question: When it was day, Jesus departed to a desolate place, but the people sought Him and tried to keep Him from leaving. What did He say to them?
options: "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well; for I was sent for this purpose."
"I must go to Jerusalem to be sacrificed."
"I go to pray alone in the mountains."
"You have heard enough, now walk in faith without me."
questions.correctAnswer: "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well; for I was sent for this purpose."
questions.explanation: Luke 4:43 (ESV): "but he said to them, 'I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well; for I was sent for this purpose.'"

key_verse_text: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty those who are oppressed,"
